hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger was small: at 00:25:22 payment-svc started a rolling deploy of v4.4.0 (#2698), and payment-svc-2 drained, leaving 3 of 4 instances (#2720). The order-service RetryPolicy for payment-svc retries immediately, up to 4 times, with backoff and jitter turned off (#2752, #2834, #2942). The short capacity dip set off those retries and the load multiplied. Payment-svc returned to 4/4 at 00:26:14 (#2809), but one second later its load shedder was active with inflight=843 at 3.2x the expected rate (#2811). The rate later reached 4.1x and 5x (#3025, #3221), and payment-svc kept rejecting /charge with 503 (#2867). Each rejection caused more immediate retries, so the loop kept itself going after capacity came back. That is why the gateway's /checkout 503s do not recover. Payment-svc served /charge in under 90ms until the rollout, so it was not slow on its own. Ruled out as unrelated: the report-cron pandas error (an earlier image), catalog-svc's third-party translation API 502/503 (affects the search path only), metrics-agent exporter drops, and a slow postgres audit_log query.

The payment-svc v4.4.0 rollout lines up with the onset, so new code could have reduced capacity. But /charge calls still succeeded during the rollout (#2738, #2754), and the shedding messages blame inbound rate (3–5x baseline), not errors in the new version. That points to retry amplification rather than a faulty release.
The third-party translation API returned 502/503 and catalog-svc opened its circuit breaker. This only affects the search path, not POST /checkout.

verdict.recommendedAction: Stop the retry storm. Turn on exponential backoff with jitter in order-service's payment-svc RetryPolicy (or turn its retries off for now) and add a retry budget or circuit breaker. To clear the backlog quickly, temporarily scale payment-svc out and/or rate-limit /checkout at the gateway. Hold further payment-svc rollouts until retries are fixed, and do future rollouts with surge capacity so instances aren't drained under load.

hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger was small: at 00:25:22 payment-svc started a rolling deploy of v4.4.0 (#2698), and payment-svc-2 drained, leaving 3 of 4 instances (#2720). The order-service RetryPolicy for payment-svc retries immediately, up to 4 times, with backoff and jitter turned off (#2752, #2834, #2942). The short capacity dip set off those retries and the load multiplied. Payment-svc returned to 4/4 at 00:26:14 (#2809), but one second later its load shedder was active with inflight=843 at 3.2x the expected rate (#2811). The rate later reached 4.1x and 5x (#3025, #3221), and payment-svc kept rejecting /charge with 503 (#2867). Each rejection caused more immediate retries, so the loop kept itself going after capacity came back. That is why the gateway's /checkout 503s do not recover. Payment-svc served /charge in under 90ms until the rollout, so it was not slow on its own. Ruled out as unrelated: the report-cron pandas error (an earlier image), catalog-svc's third-party translation API 502/503 (affects the search path only), metrics-agent exporter drops, and a slow postgres audit_log query.

The payment-svc v4.4.0 rollout lines up with the onset, so new code could have reduced capacity. But /charge calls still succeeded during the rollout (#2738, #2754), and the shedding messages blame inbound rate (3–5x baseline), not errors in the new version. That points to retry amplification rather than a faulty release.
The third-party translation API returned 502/503 and catalog-svc opened its circuit breaker. This only affects the search path, not POST /checkout.

input.recommendedAction: Stop the retry storm. Turn on exponential backoff with jitter in order-service's payment-svc RetryPolicy (or turn its retries off for now) and add a retry budget or circuit breaker. To clear the backlog quickly, temporarily scale payment-svc out and/or rate-limit /checkout at the gateway. Hold further payment-svc rollouts until retries are fixed, and do future rollouts with surge capacity so instances aren't drained under load.
